display.title: Sefirah: Why We Are Sad, and the Lesson of Rabbi Akiva's Students
display.summary_short: Why the radio show had no music during Sefirah: the days of mourning for Rabbi Akiva's students, and the lesson to respect and love every Jew.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast during Sefiras HaOmer without the usual opening music. Uncle Yossi explains that serving Hashem with joy is a mitzvah, but as Shlomo HaMelech taught, there is a time for everything, including a time to be sad. During the days between Pesach and Shavuos we hold back from celebrations: no new clothes, no new fruits that need Shehecheyanu, no haircuts. The reason is a tragedy long ago: thousands of Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague because they did not show respect to one another, and the plague ended on Lag BaOmer. These days are a time to check ourselves: do we honor others? Showing respect is a sign of Ahavas Yisroel, which leads to achdus, the unity that protects the Jewish people and will bring Moshiach.
display.lesson: Use the days of Sefirah to check that you show respect to others; Ahavas Yisroel and achdus bring Moshiach.
